thread:
incident-bot: Paging @oncall — alert: elevated 99th pct latency for /v1/generate (redwood-hosted) across pool gpu-pool-2. Metric: token_latency_99 = 850ms, baseline 220ms. Pattern: sustained since ~10:12 UTC.
Maria K: I’m on it. Seeing KV-cache miss rate spike and batch window growth in the traces.
jonathan: confirmed. Looks like continuous-batching heuristics expanded batch window to 200ms on long tail. KV cache entries for some tenants exploded.
Alex P: Any customer impact yet?
Maria K: A few medium-sized tenants seeing 5-10x token costs and slower responses. No total outage but errors up for one tenant (acme-corp) with timeouts on streaming.
Ryan S: Posting current top-level symptoms: high token_latency_99, batch_window_ms up to 220ms, kv_cache_size per-tenant up to 12GB for acme-corp.
jonathan: Logs:
```
[10:14:37] pool=gpu-pool-2 tenant=acme-corp kv_cache_items=3.2M kv_cache_size=12.1GB batch_window_ms=215 active_connections=42
[10:15:02] pool=gpu-pool-2 tenant=betaapp kv_cache_items=78k kv_cache_size=300MB batch_window_ms=190
```
Maria K: Hypothesis: new batch-window-adaptive heuristic shipped in the last runtime rollout widened windows for skewed seq-length traffic, causing repeated cache growth + more batching -> feedback loop.
Alex P: Is there a quick mitigation? Can we toggle continuous-batching off globally? That’d reduce throughput but restore latency.
jonathan: We have per-pool and per-tenant feature flags. Recommend targeted approach: disable continuous-batching for gpu-pool-2 and set per-tenant override for acme-corp while we stabilize.
sre-bot: Playbook link: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/kv-cache-batch-regressions
ops-runner: I can apply feature-flag changes. Suggest order: 1) disable CB on pool 2 canary, 2) disable for acme-corp, 3) monitor 5m, 4) rollback or staged re-enable.
Maria K: Agree. Also prepare a per-customer cache trim script to evict excessive KV entries while flag is rolling.
jonathan: Commands I’ll run (dry-run then execute):
```
# dry run show
redwoodctl feature-flag show continuous-batching --scope=pool:gpu-pool-2
redwoodctl feature-flag show continuous-batching --scope=tenant:acme-corp

# disable pool
redwoodctl feature-flag set continuous-batching --off --scope=pool:gpu-pool-2 --reason="emergency KV cache feedback loop"

# per-tenant override
redwoodctl feature-flag set continuous-batching --off --scope=tenant:acme-corp --reason="mitigation"
```
ops-runner: running dry-run now.
ops-runner: dry-run output: pool current=true tenant acme-corp=true (inherited).
ops-runner: applying pool-level disable...
incident-bot: Deploy event: feature-flag continuous-batching disabled on pool:gpu-pool-2 (by ops-runner) at 1782012601.
Maria K: Confirming metrics — batch_window_ms falling to 30-50ms on pool-2 within 30s.
Ryan S: KV cache miss rate still high but kv_cache_size for acme-corp plateaued.
jonathan: Now applying per-tenant disable for acme-corp.
ops-runner: applied per-tenant disable for acme-corp. Incident-bot confirmed: 1782012745.
Alex P: Good. Any downstream issues from disabling? We might see increased GPU utilization from more smaller batches.
Maria K: Expect uptick in GPU utilization ~5-10%, but latency OOM should drop. We have headroom on pool-2 for now.
jonathan: Running cache-trim for acme-corp to free KV memory:
```
python tools/kv_trim.py --tenant acme-corp --target-size 1GB --mode=evict-lru
```
ops-runner: started trim job (job-id 8f3a). ETA ~45s.
Ryan S: Post-trim snapshot: kv_cache_size acme-corp = 980MB, items 260k. Latency 99th now 230ms — much improved.
sre-bot: Noting customer impact: acme-corp experienced increased token latency and occasional stream timeouts from 10:12–10:27 UTC. Escalation: Customer success pinged.
Alex P: Do we want to open a support ticket and proactively notify acme-corp?
Maria K: Yes, send note: summarise cause, mitigation, and next steps. I’ll draft.
jonathan: Next steps: 1) keep CB disabled on gpu-pool-2 until next runtime patch, 2) create a change to the heuristic (cap max batch window at 100ms and add mem guard on per-tenant KV growth), 3) run targeted canary on pool-3 in staging.
ops-runner: I’ll schedule config rollback window if needed.
incident-bot: Incident update: Severity=SEV3, status=mitigated for primary impact, tagged "kv-cache-batch-regression", lead=@Maria K, oncall=@jonathan.
Maria K: Handing to infra oncall for follow-ups. @ryan can you lead postmortem section on detection and metric thresholds?
Ryan S: Will do. Drafting notes and collecting traces/graphs.
Alex P: Thanks team. Follow-up: add per-customer override to self-serve console so Support can toggle for large customers without infra involvement.
jonathan: Filed feature request: PLAT-1029.
Maria K: Closing handoff — if any recurrences ping this thread. Good job moving fast. :thumbsup:
